Maluku has 40 seasonal zones (ZOM): 12 monsoonal, 21 equatorial and 7 'local'. The local type is reversed from the monsoon pattern, with peak rain around June-August. For example, Amahai has its wet season in April-September.
facts.source_name: BMKG Buku Prakiraan Musim Hujan 2022/2023; academic study for Amahai

facts.claim: Maluku scored 160.03 on BNPB IRBI 2023, the second-highest disaster risk index of any province.
The Weber Deep in the Banda Sea, about 7.2 km deep (7,440 m in the 1929-30 Snellius survey), is the deepest point in Indonesian waters and the deepest ocean point on Earth outside a trench.
facts.source_name: Pownall, Hall & Lister (peer-reviewed); Snellius expedition record

facts.claim: North Maluku has highly active volcanoes, for example Ibu on Halmahera, which Badan Geologi monitors.

regions.robotics_relevance: Maluku is almost entirely ocean (92%), made of scattered small islands with deep seas, high seismic and volcanic risk, and a rain season reversed from the rest of Indonesia. It suits marine robotics (AUV/ROV, deep-sea), fisheries IoT, inter-island drone logistics, and off-grid, salt-exposed sensors. A country-wide test program can also run here in Indonesia's 'off-season'.

facts.claim: The Indonesian part of New Guinea (Papua provinces) covers about 412,000-421,000 km2. Sources disagree, and the province figures do not add up exactly.

Indonesia's tropical glacier at Puncak Sudirman/Jayawijaya shrank to 0.11-0.16 km2 in Nov 2024, from 0.23 km2 in 2022. About 4 m of ice thickness remained, against 32 m in 2010. BMKG expects it to disappear within a few years.
Puncak Jaya (Carstensz Pyramid) is Indonesia's highest peak at 4,884 m asl.
Southwest Papua has the most islands of any province (about 3,022), and West Papua has about 1,498.
Papua has about 3 million ha of peatland, mostly in the southern lowlands.
In the 2026 El Nino dry season BMKG reported smoke over Papua Pegunungan, Papua Tengah and Papua Selatan. On 13 Sep 2026, Papua and Maluku together had 200 high-confidence hotspots.
Sentani (Papua) sometimes exceeds 36 C, the highest daily maximum in BMKG's May 2020 heat note.

regions.robotics_relevance: Papua is the most extreme terrain gradient in Indonesia: tropical coast and swamp, lowland peat, and highlands above 4,000 m with Indonesia's only (vanishing) glacier, along with very sparse roads and grid. It suits long-endurance and high-altitude drones, off-grid, satellite-connected sensors, climate and glacier instrumentation, mining autonomy, and remote-logistics robotics.

facts.claim: BIG counts 17,380 islands in 2024, up from 17,374 in 2023. Only named, coordinate-verified islands are counted, the gazetteer is updated every year, and 63 new islands were added in Bangka Belitung, SE Sulawesi, North Maluku and West Kalimantan. Older figures (17,504; 16,671 registered at the UN) are still widely quoted.
facts.source_name: Badan Informasi Geospasial (BIG), Rilis Jumlah Pulau

facts.claim: Coastline: the 2018 national territorial reference data (BIG with Pushidrosal TNI AL, launched by Kemenko Maritim on 10 Aug 2018) gives 108,000 km, and the KKP Renstra 2025-2029 uses the same figure. The older BIG/KKP 2017 figure of 99,093 km is still common, and 104,000 km and 110,000 km also appear.
facts.source_name: KKP Renstra Ditjen PDSPKP 2025-2029; Mongabay on the 2018 data release

facts.claim: Under the 2018 reference data, Indonesia's total waters cover about 6.4 million km2: inland plus archipelagic waters 3.11 million, territorial sea 0.29 million, and an EEZ of about 3.0 million. The total territory (land plus water) is about 8.3 million km2, against roughly 1.9 million km2 of land, so sea is about 3x land. A KKP report instead uses 5.8 million km2 of marine waters.
facts.value: ~6.4 million km2 waters vs ~1.9 million km2 land
facts.source_name: Kemenko Maritim/BIG/Pushidrosal via Mongabay; KKP LKj

facts.claim: Island-rich provinces are mostly maritime: Southwest Papua about 3,022, Riau Islands about 2,028, Central Sulawesi about 1,572 and Maluku about 1,388.
BIG says islands change through abrasion, sedimentation and merging with other land. Coasts are therefore physically dynamic, and the coastline figure depends on the mapping method.

regions.robotics_relevance: With over 100,000 km of tropical coast, salt spray and high humidity (>80% RH), constant 27-28 C, and three times more sea than land, Indonesia is a natural lab for corrosion and IP-rating endurance, marine and underwater robotics, port automation, aquaculture and fisheries IoT, and inter-island drone and vessel autonomy. Kepri sits next to Singapore, which makes it a convenient maritime test base for foreign firms.

national_facts.claim: Number of islands (BIG, named and coordinated)
Coastline length per the 2018 national reference data (BIG + Pushidrosal), as used by KKP. Figures differ by source and method.
national_facts.source_name: KKP Renstra 2025-2029; Kemenko Maritim release via Mongabay

national_facts.claim: Total territory and waters: about 8.3 million km2 total, of which about 6.4 million km2 is water (incl. EEZ ~3.0 million) and about 1.9 million km2 is land. BIG elsewhere gives 1,922,570 km2 of land and 3,257,483 km2 of waters excluding the EEZ.
Indonesia has 127 active volcanoes (about 13% of the world's) out of roughly 500 volcanoes. About 45 million people live near active volcanoes, and Badan Geologi runs about 74-75 observation posts.
national_facts.source_name: Kementerian ESDM press release No. 431.Pers/04/SJI/2024 (7 Aug 2024)

national_facts.claim: National mean air temperature was 27.5 C in 2024 (normal 1991-2020: 26.7 C; anomaly +0.8 C; 117 stations), the warmest year since 1981. The 2025 mean was 27.05 C.
Relative humidity is high all year. BMKG cites an average of about 70-90% (April 2025), and >80-100% across most of Indonesia in a May 2020 note.
national_facts.source_name: BMKG press release; BMKG via CNBC

national_facts.claim: BMKG defines seasons per seasonal zone (699 ZOM, 1991-2020 normals). The rainy season starts when one dasarian (10 days) has >=50 mm and the next two dasarian also do. Rainfall falls into three regimes: monsoonal (wet ~Nov-Apr), equatorial (two peaks) and local (reversed, wet ~Jun-Aug in parts of Maluku and Papua).

2026/2027 outlook: under a very strong El Nino plus a positive IOD, the rainy season is late in 529 ZOM (61.08% of land area) and shorter than normal in 482 ZOM. Onset is mostly November-December 2026, with the peak in December 2026-February 2027.
National peatland area is 13.43 million ha (BBSDLP/Kementan 2019 map at 1:50,000, SNI 7925:2019). KLH cited 13.36 million ha in 2025, and the older 2011 map gave about 14.9 million ha.

The forest and land fire (haze) season usually runs July-October and peaks in August-September, with the worst years under El Nino. BMKG's 2026 priority provinces are Riau, Jambi, South Sumatra, West Kalimantan and Central Kalimantan.

caveats: BPS's land-area and islands-per-province tables (bps.go.id) return 403 to automated fetches or render only with JavaScript, so per-island land areas come from media citing BPS and are low/medium confidence. Before publishing, open BPS 'Luas Daerah dan Jumlah Pulau Menurut Provinsi' (https://www.bps.go.id/id/statistics-table/3/VUZwV01tSlpPVlpsWlRKbmMxcFhhSGhEVjFoUFFUMDkjMw==/luas-daerah-dan-jumlah-pulau-menurut-provinsi.html) in a browser and check them. My Sumatra figure (~480,800 km2) is my own sum of province areas.

Coastline length is contested: 108,000 km (2018 BIG+Pushidrosal reference, used by KKP), 99,093 km (older BIG/KKP 2017), and also 104,000 or 110,000 km. On the site, say 'about 108,000 km (2018 national reference)' or 'over 99,000 km'.
Island counts change every year (BIG 17,380 in 2024; 17,504 and 16,671 are older figures). Province island counts differ between BPS-cited sources (Maluku 1,388 vs 1,412).
Sea area depends on the definition: about 6.4 million km2 including the EEZ (2018 reference), 5.8 million km2 (KKP report), or 3.26 million km2 excluding the EEZ (BIG). Say which one you mean.
The 127 active volcanoes figure is official (ESDM/Badan Geologi), but I found no official breakdown per island. Do not show per-region volcano counts.

For each region's 'climate' line, pull specific station normals from BMKG Data Online (dataonline.bmkg.go.id) or provincial Staklim bulletins.
